title: Autogenerated lightweight smoke profiles and publish telemetry contract
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary:
We need a fast, automated ‘smoke profile’ that runs during model onboarding and after minor model variant rollouts to detect large regressions in latency or cost before running the full Verified Performance Profile (VPP) pipeline. The smoke profile should be cheap, deterministic across regions, and produce a signed short-form artifact plus telemetry contract that can gate publishing to the canonical profile registry.

Goals:
- Create an autogenerated, lightweight smoke-profile suite (<= 1% of full VPP compute) that focuses on high-sensitivity checks for latency tail regressions, gross throughput drops, and cost-per-token anomalies.
- Emit a compact signed artifact (smoke-signature.json) with normalized latency/throughput/cost fields and a telemetry contract describing required metrics and thresholds.
- Integrate smoke checks as a gating step in the existing publish pipeline so that a model variant that fails smoke cannot proceed to full verification without an opt-in override and documented justification.
- Keep false-positive rate low by normalizing for region/hardware and using deterministic synthetic prompts.

Non-goals:
- Not replacing full Verified Performance Profiles. The smoke profile is an early-warning, low-cost gate only.
- Not implementing full per-customer workload shadowing in this iteration.

Success metrics:
- Detect >= 90% of VPP failures that would have led to rollback within 24 hours if smoke had not run (measured via backtests on the last 6 months of onboarding changes).
- Average smoke run cost < 1% of full VPP run.
- Gate prevents at least 40% of candidate variants from being auto-published when they have significant regressions during staging.

Acceptance criteria:
- A reproducible smoke runner that can be invoked from the onboarding pipeline (CLI + REST API).
- Signed smoke artifact schema defined and validated in CI (schema published in confluence link).
- Pipeline integration: failures stop publish and create a ticket with auto-populated diagnostics.
- Smoke telemetry contract added to the telemetry registry and enforced by the verifier.

Design proposal (high level):
1) Smoke runner generation: onboarding job assembles a deterministic, small set of prompts per model family. Prompts are designed to exercise common attention/long-context patterns and worst-case short sequences for KV cache behavior.
2) Normalization layer: raw latency and throughput are normalized by hardware profile (GPU type, quantization), and region latency baselines are subtracted. Cost-per-token normalized by sequence-length distribution.
3) Thresholding: thresholds per metric derived from historical variance windows and per-family baselines. Thresholds are intentionally permissive but catch >30% regressions and big tail spikes.
4) Signed artifact: smoke-signature.json includes: model_id, model_version, baseline_anchor, metrics: {latency_p50, latency_p95, throughput_rps, cost_per_token_scaled}, pass_fail, signer_id, signature_hex. Artifact signing uses existing profile signing key material (managed by release/ops).
5) Telemetry contract: JSON contract listing expected metrics, units, aggregation windows, and alerting hooks (dashboard ids and alert ids). The verifier enforces that any published VPP has a preceding smoke-signature or an approved override.

Pipeline integration and rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (alpha, internal): wire smoke runner into staging-onboard jobs for a subset of low-risk model families. Collect metrics and tune thresholds. Owners: ENG-serving (runtime), PM-owner (Ava), Design: n/a.
- Phase 2 (beta, expanded): enable gating in canonical publish CI for all onboards flagged as ‘auto-publish’. Notify release channels on fails and create auto-tickets linking diagnostics.
- Phase 3 (enforced): block publishes by default unless smoke passes or a documented override is present; roll to Dedicated and Private onboarding flows.

Monitoring, dashboards and alerts:
- New dashboard: "Smoke Profiles — Recent Runs" (links: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/smoke-profiles).
- Alerts: smoke-regression-critical (fires when latency_p95 increases > 2x anchor) and smoke-cost-exceed (fires when cost_per_token_scaled > 1.5x baseline).
- Observatory hook: any smoke fail auto-populates an onboarding ticket with the raw traces, kernel selection snapshot, and the signed artifact.

Migration and compatibility:
- Legacy onboards without smoke artifacts remain supported for 30 days; we will run a background smoke scan and attempt to auto-generate artifacts for recent onboards.
- Backwards compatibility: verifier will accept either smoke-signature or explicit manual signoff until enforcement date.

Security and signing:
- Use existing signing service. Keys rotated per release-cadence. Signing operations audited in release logs.
- No user data is used in smoke prompts — only synthetic/deterministic prompts to avoid PII leakage.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Prompt selection strategy: seed-based synthetic prompts vs. small curated corpus from anonymized production traces. Trade-off: realism vs. privacy and determinism.
- Threshold strategy: fixed multiplier vs. adaptive thresholds based on rolling windows. Adaptive reduces false positives but is more complex to reason about.
- Opt-in override flow: who can override? Should override require two approvers for high-impact models?

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence spec (draft): https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/PM/Smoke+Profile+Spec
- Design doc / schema PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-profiles/pull/783
- Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.internal/smoke-profiles

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives causing onboarding friction: mitigate by running a 3-week shadow period and adjusting thresholds; provide clear diagnostics to reduce investigatory cost.
- Signature key compromise: rotate keys and require multi-sig for release-level keys.
- Overhead on onboarding pipeline: ensure smoke runner is heavily parallelized and budgeted as a small fixed-cost step.

Owner and contacts:
- PM: Ava Martinez (creator)
- Eng lead: Liam Chen (assignee)
- Runtime owner: Priya Desai
- Release engineering: Marco Ruiz

Next steps (immediate):
1) Engineering spike: implement smoke runner prototype and smoke-signature emitter (2 wks).
2) Run backtests against last six months of onboarding events and tune thresholds (1 week).
3) Create dashboard and CI gating job (2 wks).
